newsitem.title: USA: ARCO unveils new oil tanker class.
newsitem.headline: ARCO unveils new oil tanker class.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co. on Tuesday unveiled a new design for the huge oil tankers it will run between Alaska and its West Coast refineries beginning in 2000.
New Orleans-based Avondale Industries Inc will build two 125,000 dead weight ton (dwt) crude carriers for ARCO's shipping division at a cost of $332 million. The first will go into service in 200O.
"These ships...set entirely new standards for safety at sea," Bill Rusnack, president of ARCO Products Co., the parent company of ARCO Marine Inc, said in a statement.
The ships, dubbed the "Millenium" class, are a response to stricter laws and heightened environmental awareness following the Exxon Valdez oil spill in 1989, the company said.

The ships comply with double-hull standards mandated by the Oil Pollution Act of 1990, ARCO said, and will have a backup engine, two propellers, and several other features that give them greater strength and maneuverability in Alaska's rough seas.
"It's the first of its kind with all these features in one ship," said ARCO Marine spokesman Richard Verches.
ARCO has the option to commission three more tankers from Avondale, depending on future overseas production, Verches said.
The tankers will carry about one million barrels of crude oil over 2,400 miles from Alaska's Valdez oil terminal to ARCO's refinery in Washington state, the company said.
